body:
Independent fresh-context review of the exact head `1d36eebdf7cafa1f9e0c83037abebb3db262127f`, by two models of different families, each in a fresh read-only context that did not author the change.

**Verdict: APPROVE — no P0 findings, no P1 findings.**

What the review verified:

- A request with `stream_options.include_usage` gets a last chunk in the OpenAI shape: an empty `choices` list, the object `chat.completion.chunk`, the id, the model and the time of the answer it reports on, and the counts of the prompt and the answer apart. The chunk is the last one before `[DONE]`, and the finish-reason chunk still arrives.
- The count of an answer is the same whatever the upstream split the text into. The review drove the wrapper over the same answer split at 1, 3, 7 and 1000 characters: the count equals the count of the whole text in every case.
- The counter keeps the text it carries bounded, so an answer with a very long unbroken run does not grow the buffer without bound.
- A request without `stream_options.include_usage` gets no usage chunk, and a `stream_options` of the wrong type is ignored.
- The last commit merges `main` into the branch and changes nothing in the tree, so the content the review covers is the content that will be merged.

The reviews drove three rounds of fixes, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-change code: the usage chunk carried an id and a model of its own, so it did not belong to the completion it reported on; the count of a streamed answer depended on where the upstream split the text; and the time of the usage chunk was its own, so it was off by the time the upstream took to answer.

The changelog says that the token counts of a non-streamed answer change with this, because they were counted as a quarter of the characters before.

The `CI` and `dco` checks are green on this head.
